clue.text: Opening meeting of wise women is left divided

indicators.note: opening something up just past its first letter makes room for another letter to go inside

blocks.note: a coven is a gathering of witches, the wise women of folklore
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A gathering of wise women begins with its members split into two camps.
explanation.walkthrough: COVEN is opened after its first letter and L slips in: C-L-OVEN. 'Opening' reads as a noun describing the meeting, but it is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloven is the old past participle of cleave, meaning split in two, as in a cloven hoof.

clue.text: This woman staying in, wearing clothes that didn’t match

indicators.note: whatever stays in somewhere is kept inside it, so this goes within another piece

blocks.note: clad means dressed, wearing clothes
the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman stays home dressed in an outfit whose pieces don't go together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This woman' is simply the pronoun she; 'wearing clothes' is one adjective meaning dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours or garments that clash look wrong together, so clashed is a past-tense verb for failing to go well together.

clue.text: Like Humpty-Dumpty, round, as described by poet

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw a line around it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses
a round shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A poet describes the nursery-rhyme figure Humpty-Dumpty as round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Described' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round: OVID goes round O. Humpty-Dumpty is traditionally drawn as an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, and the nursery-rhyme character is always pictured as a large egg.

clue.text: In greatest distress, perhaps a hand

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; the phrase 'in extremity' means in greatest distress

blocks.note: first meaning: a state of extreme hardship
second meaning: a limb's far end, such as a hand or foot

explanation.surface: Someone in dire trouble reaches out, perhaps with a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning only works with 'in' in front: to be in extremity is to be in dire straits. 'Perhaps' signals that a hand is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands and feet are the body's outermost parts, called extremities; the same word names a condition of severe hardship or danger.

clue.text: One making argument presented girl with tear-jerker

indicators.note: something jerked is yanked about roughly, so these letters are jolted out of order

blocks.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman formally presented to society
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl was given a weepy film to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear-jerker' looks like one word meaning a sad film, but it splits: TEAR is the fodder and 'jerker' the signal. A deb was traditionally presented at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A debater is someone who takes part in formal argument, putting a case for or against a motion.

clue.text: Last month past noon several sides joined for this

blocks.note: December is the final month of the year, abbreviated Dec
ago means in the past, gone by
N is an abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Last month, just after midday, several teams came together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' suggests teams joining up; in the definition they are the straight edges of a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a flat polygon made of ten straight edges meeting at ten corners.

clue.text: South African admitting wife is a violinist

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece takes another inside

blocks.note: a Boer is a South African of Dutch descent
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A South African man confesses that his wife plays the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: BOER takes in W. The answer is read as 'one who bows', rhyming with 'goer', not the garden arbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist draws a bow across the strings, so a playful coinage calls such a player one who bows.

clue.text: Deter dust blowing around legal document

indicators.note: things blown around are scattered by the wind and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An official paper keeps windblown dust away.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of the first two words rearrange into the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trust deed is the formal instrument that sets up a trust and names its trustees and beneficiaries.

clue.text: In administration, a number of companies’ books are missing

indicators.note: whatever is missing has been taken away, so these letters drop out

blocks.note: an army regiment is made up of several companies of soldiers
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Several firms have gone into administration and their account books have vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Companies' and 'books' suggest business accounts; here they are military units and the New Testament. REGIMENT loses NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a government or system of rule, the body that administers a country.

clue.text: Whites here virtually too sick

indicators.note: virtually means almost but not quite, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: also means too, as well
sick is slang for brilliant, as is ace

explanation.surface: Pale people here feel almost too ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whites' suggests pale faces but means white wines. 'Sick' is youth slang for excellent, hence ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French region bordering Germany is famous for white wines such as Riesling and Gewurztraminer.

clue.text: Carrying out mission, working as co-pilot

indicators.note: working letters are set in motion and rearranged, as a machine's parts move

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A second pilot flies on an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mission' sounds military or aeronautical; here it is a religious calling, as with the apostles.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were sent out to spread the faith; apostolic describes that evangelising, missionary task.

clue.text: Twisted wide part of climbing frame

blocks.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wide
a rung is a crossbar of a ladder or climbing frame

explanation.surface: A bent, broad bar on a playground climbing frame.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, recorded as W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrung is the past tense of wring, to squeeze by turning, as with washing.

clue.text: German philosopher shortly holding Dutch is a barrier

indicators.note: shortly here means cut short, so the name loses its last letter
holding something means having it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: Hegel was the German idealist philosopher
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A German thinker soon finds the Dutch language hard to get past.
explanation.walkthrough: HEGEL loses its last letter to give HEGE, which then holds D.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a row of dense bushes planted to form a boundary, keeping animals or people out.

clue.text: VP once almost hit badly by mass set of instructions

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped
something done badly comes out wrong, so these letters end up disordered

blocks.note: Al Gore was US Vice President under Bill Clinton
taken as written, to be rearranged
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A former vice president was badly struck by a crowd while following a set of orders.
explanation.walkthrough: VP is Vice President; the 'once' points to a former holder, Al Gore, cut to ALGOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An algorithm is a precise sequence of steps for solving a problem, especially one followed by a computer.

clue.text: Go through cases for refuse

blocks.note: first meaning: list a noun's grammatical forms, as in Latin
second meaning: politely say no

explanation.surface: Someone sorts through boxes looking for rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the noun meaning rubbish, and 'cases' as boxes; both are misdirections. Cases are grammatical: nominative, accusative and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar one declines a noun by reciting its case endings; in ordinary speech to decline an offer is to turn it down.

clue.text: Took charge of international and got old boy to leave

indicators.note: whatever leaves goes away, so these letters are removed

blocks.note: a cap is a player selected for a national team
obtained means got, acquired
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A national team player led the side and forced out a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: OBTAINED loses OB to leave TAINED. In British sport an international player is said to have won a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: To captain is to lead a team or ship, so captained is a past-tense verb for having been in command.

clue.text: Growth centres in new capitals sure to miss out on relaxation

indicators.note: missing out on something means going without it, so those letters are left out

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
UC stands for upper case, meaning capital letters
leisure is free time for relaxing
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: New capital cities, keen to grow, are certain to lack leisure time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' suggests cities; it is UC, the printer's abbreviation for upper case. LEISURE minus SURE leaves LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is a central core around which things gather or develop, so nuclei are points from which growth spreads.

clue.text: Following complaints upfront are still not well fed periodically

indicators.note: upfront means at the very front, so only the opening letter is kept
periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to lie is to stay still, as in lie still
the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: After grumbling at the start, people are still going hungry now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a linking preposition but is the noun definition. 'Are still' means lie, as in lying motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A business's following is its regular customers or patrons, which is exactly what its clientele means.

clue.text: Mister not active? Even more so

definitions.note: stands for 'even more active', picking up the clue's own word

indicators.note: not having something means going without it, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: a mister is a device that sprays a fine mist, a sprayer
A is the grammatical abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: Is the gentleman idle? Quite the opposite: he is livelier still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a title but is a spray bottle. The definition refers back: more so than active, i.e. more spry.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means nimble and lively, so its comparative describes someone still more energetic than merely active.

clue.text: Avoid damaging muscle during relaxation

indicators.note: during means within the time of something, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: rest is relaxation
pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Advice to stay clear of pulling a muscle while resting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoid damaging' reads as part of the fitness advice, but it is the definition, in the sense of respecting boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect the environment or a rule is to leave it unharmed or unbroken, so the verb covers refraining from harm.

clue.text: Gale in valley, but not a drop

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another
not having the letter means it is removed

blocks.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England
a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A storm blows through a valley, yet no rain falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' suggests a raindrop; it is the verb meaning decrease.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to grow gradually smaller in number or size, the same as a fall or decline.

clue.text: Hurled plate (taken from cupboard, is customary)

indicators.note: taken from means lifted out of the words that follow, so the letters are inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Throwing crockery out of the cupboard is normal, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The parentheses make the plate sound like crockery flung in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is a heavy disc thrown in athletics, so a plate-like object hurled for distance.

clue.text: Most mysterious English lake with a bed of stone

indicators.note: in a down entry, the bed is the bottom, so this piece goes at the end

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Lake Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes
st is the abbreviation for the stone, a British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: The strangest of English lakes has a stony floor.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is an imperial unit of body weight still used in Britain, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, so its superlative describes whatever is the most uncanny or baffling.

clue.text: Makes sense to have another drink

blocks.note: first meaning: is logical, hangs together
second meaning, read as two words: a further sup, or sip, is added

explanation.surface: It seems reasonable to order one more round.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning needs splitting: to add a sup, where a sup is a mouthful of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: When a story or argument is consistent and believable, people say it adds up; the phrase is an idiom for being logical.

clue.text: Having rejected help with new series, a mark for each of the Brontës

definitions.text: a mark for each of the Brontës

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so these letters go the other way
making something new means remaking it, so these letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: aid means help
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning down assistance for a new book series, each Brontë sister gets a grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' suggests a grade; it is the two dots over the final E of Brontë.
explanation.definitionFit: The two dots over the e in Brontë form a diaeresis, the accent showing a vowel is sounded separately.

clue.text: Follower of religion that elevates a head of state

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters makes them read from the bottom up

blocks.note: taken as written
a tsar was the ruler of Russia

explanation.surface: A religious believer whose faith exalts a national leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: Rastafarians revere Haile Selassie, Emperor of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta is an adherent of Rastafarianism, the faith that arose in Jamaica in the 1930s.

clue.text: Nothing cooling in nice jug? Later

indicators.note: nothing of something means none of it remains, so those letters go

blocks.note: taken as written
ice is used for cooling drinks
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: No ice in the pretty jug? Maybe add some afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: NICE minus ICE leaves N, followed by EWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something later in date is more recent, and newer likewise describes what came after.

clue.text: After wicket robust thrash

indicators.note: coming after means following behind, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wicket
hale means healthy and strong

explanation.surface: Having taken a wicket, a strong batting side hits out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whale' here is the verb, informal for beating hard, not the sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To whale on someone is informal for hitting them hard and repeatedly, which is to thrash them.

clue.text: Updates phone and drives into ground to be picked up

indicators.note: picking up a sound means catching it by ear, so the word is spoken

blocks.note: to sink a post is to drive it into the ground

explanation.surface: Someone updates their mobile and also hammers posts into the earth, to be collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' pretends to mean collected, as a phone might be.
explanation.definitionFit: To sync a phone is to synchronise it with another device, bringing its data up to date.

clue.text: List non-British food additive consumed

indicators.note: non means without, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: an E-number is a code for an approved food additive in Europe
B is the abbreviation for British
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Name every foreign additive that was eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: E-numbers are the European codes printed on food labels for additives such as preservatives and colourings.
explanation.definitionFit: To enumerate is to name items one by one, which is what compiling a list involves.

clue.text: It’s something to hear selected actors at school

blocks.note: a pod is a group of whales or dolphins, like a school
the cast is the set of actors chosen for a production

explanation.surface: Worth listening to: the chosen performers in a school play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests a place of learning; it is a group of sea creatures. The piece it gives comes first despite being clued last.
explanation.definitionFit: A podcast is an audio programme you download and listen to, so it is literally something to listen to.

clue.text: What is in most excellent order?

indicators.note: being in something means sitting within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: best means most excellent
eh is an exclamation asking 'what?'

explanation.surface: A question about which item is in perfect condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' looks like the start of a question; it is EH, the puzzled interjection.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or instruction, as in 'at the king's behest'.
